transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-11
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (Redwood SE), Dana Ruiz (Meridian Head of ML), Tom Wallace (Meridian Cloud Architect), Priya Kaur (Meridian Platform Eng), Evan Shaw (Meridian SRE)

Summary:
Quick scoping session to map Meridian's SLA and throughput needs to a concrete POC plan. Focus: define workload signature (QPS, concurrency, token distribution), success criteria (latency budgets, error rates, cost thresholds), and benchmark plan + timeline. Several security/compliance checkpoints (SOC2, KMS, VPC) discussed.

Topics:
- Workload telemetry & capture
- QPS / concurrency patterns and burst behavior
- Input/output token distributions and percentile behavior
- Benchmark harness and KPIs (p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/second, cost/unit)
- Pilot timeline and gating criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for carving out time, um let's do quick intros, real short. I'm alex, AE focused on infra customers at Redwood, jordan and maya will handle the technical runbook.
[00:18] Dana Ruiz: hi, i'm dana, head of ml at meridian. we run a chat assistant and doc summarization pipelines - mostly synchronous calls from our app.
[00:28] Tom Wallace: tom here, cloud architect, we'll provide logs and coordinate the pilot infra.
[00:36] Alex Chen: cool. goal today is to map your current traffic pattern to a POC that proves we can meet your latency and cost targets. can we start with current qps and concurrency?
[00:52] Priya Kaur: average qps is about 18 sustained during the day, peaks to ~240 for 60-120 seconds during marketing blasts. concurrency varies; backend uses 100 worker threads but effective concurrent model calls are usually 40-60.
[01:09] Jordan Patel: 18 sustained / 240 burst - got it. what's the typical request length and response size, token-wise?
[01:19] Dana Ruiz: inputs are short: 8-40 tokens usually, but we have long form summarization that can be 800-1200 input tokens once an hour. outputs: chat tends to be 40-120 tokens, summarization outputs 300-700 tokens.
[01:37] Maya Lopez: ok that's a mixed distribution - so we'll need to design a mixed-profile benchmark. can you share percentile breakdowns? p50/p90 for tokens?
[01:46] Dana Ruiz: i can get that, i think p50 input ~18 tokens, p90 ~120 because of the long summaries, output p50 ~60 p90 ~420. i'll share telemetry.
[01:57] Evan Shaw: one nuance - our app front door uses lambda edge and we see cold starts sometimes, which spike latency. we care about application-level p95 under 800ms for chat.
[02:08] Alex Chen: good callout. is that 800ms end-to-end or model-only?
[02:12] Evan Shaw: end-to-end from frontend to response top-of-page. model-only we'd like p95 under 350ms ideally.
[02:20] Jordan Patel: perfect. success criteria suggestion: model-only p95 <= 350ms for chat profile, and for summarization model-only p95 <= 1.2s with cost per 1k tokens under your target - what's your cost target?
[02:35] Dana Ruiz: we're targeting less than $0.70 per 1k output tokens across workloads, averaged monthly.
[02:44] Maya Lopez: ok we'll map quantization and batching settings to hit that. one question: will this be hosted or do you need private/vpc on-prem constraints?
[02:54] Tom Wallace: we prefer VPC private deployment for data residency, but for the pilot we can try hosted with a VPC peering setup if that's faster.
[03:04] Alex Chen: we can do a hosted pilot with VPC peering and customer-managed keys, then show an on-prem checklist. for compliance - SOC2 and ISO?
[03:13] Priya Kaur: SOC2 report is required for procurement, and we need KMS integration and audit logs.
[03:20] Alex Chen: noted. we'll share our SOC2 and KMS integration doc.
[03:26] Jordan Patel: digging into traffic shape - bursts of 240 qps for 1-2 minutes. do those originate from fan-out (many users) or queue drain?
[03:35] Dana Ruiz: it's a mix. marketing push causes many users to open chat simultaneously - mostly fan-out. we also have nightly batch summaries that create steady long-form load.
[03:45] Jordan Patel: that matters for autoscaling and batching; fan-out needs low tail latency. our runtime supports continuous batching + per-tenant caching (KV cache) but high fan-out reduces batching efficiency.
[03:55] Evan Shaw: how do you handle fallback? if dedicated capacity is saturated, do you burst to hosted?
[03:59] Alex Chen: yes, policy-based routing can fallback to compatible model variants or to hosted burst capacity to keep p95 bounded; we'll show config in the playbook.
[04:07] Tom Wallace: great. for benchmarking we want to capture realistic client behavior so we're not over-optimistic. how do you recommend we capture traffic?
[04:15] Maya Lopez: simplest is a 72-hour export of request logs with payload size and timing. we ingest and synthesize a workload signature: qps time-series, concurrency distribution, input/output token histograms, and cold-start incidence.
[04:27] Dana Ruiz: we can pull that. any privacy concerns with sending payloads? should we sanitize?
[04:33] Alex Chen: yes please sanitize PII—if you can send token counts and anonymized payloads that's perfect. we only need payload shapes for model benchmarking.
[04:42] Jordan Patel: on metrics, propose we measure: model-only p50/p95/p99, end-to-end p50/p95, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, and a success boolean for each scenario.
[04:56] Dana Ruiz: accepted. what about concurrency vs batching size tradeoffs? we want to understand latency cost curves.
[05:04] Jordan Patel: we'll run param sweep: concurrency levels (10, 40, 80, 160), batching targets (max batch size 8/16/32), and KV cache hit rates simulated (0%, 30%, 70%). this gives a surface to pick settings.
[05:20] Evan Shaw: timeline realistic? we need results before procurement meeting end of month. procurement meeting is 2026-05-05.
[05:27] Alex Chen: workable. proposed schedule: you provide telemetry by 2026-04-14; we run pilot 2026-04-17 to 04-19 (48 hours of targeted runs + 24 hours soak); results and cost scenarios 2026-04-22; show-and-tell + procurement pack 2026-04-25.
[05:41] Priya Kaur: does pilot need access to our prod? we'd prefer a mirrored environment with sampled traffic.
[05:48] Maya Lopez: we can run against a replay of sampled traffic in your staging environment, or run synthetic traffic against hosted endpoints with the same signature. both are supported.
[05:58] Tom Wallace: security: SAML SSO is required for console access and audit logs must go to our splunk instance. also HSM/KMS for keys.
[06:07] Alex Chen: we support SAML, SSO provisioning, and can ship audit logs to your splunk via syslog or S3 + ingestion. HSM for key wrapping is part of our private offering; for hosted we offer customer-managed KMS.
[06:18] Dana Ruiz: one procurement question - are there minimum commitments for Dedicated?
[06:22] Alex Chen: Dedicated typically has a monthly commit, but you can start with hosted pilot then move to a reserved capacity conversation post-pilot. we'll include illustrative pricing scenarios.
[06:30] Evan Shaw: on monitoring during pilot - will you provide dashboards and traces?
[06:34] Jordan Patel: yes, we'll provide per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and KV cache hit traces. we'll also instrument tail latency and p99 for each model variant.
[06:44] Dana Ruiz: curious about quantization impacts for summarization: does 4-bit quant hurt long-form output quality?
[06:49] Maya Lopez: it can for some models; we'll test both fp16/8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants and run an eval suite with your prompt set to measure ROUGE/semantic similarity and hallucination rates.
[06:59] Tom Wallace: what's needed from our side to run the benchmark?
[07:01] Alex Chen: deliverables: 72-hour telemetry export (sanitized), sample prompts and evaluation set, access to staging or a replay mechanism, and a list of success criteria thresholds.
[07:12] Priya Kaur: we'll assemble those. one more - in case pilot shows p95 slightly above target, what's the path?
[07:18] Jordan Patel: we'd iterate on batching/quantization and, if needed, move to larger instance families or Dedicated capacity. fallback strategies maintain availability. we'll present cost delta for each option in the report.
[07:30] Dana Ruiz: ok. procurement will ask competitor comparatives. can you show latency/cost vs Anthropic and Vertex?
[07:36] Alex Chen: we can provide benchmark-style comparatives using public profiles; we'll label them approximate. vendor names are fine to include in the procurement pack.
[07:44] Evan Shaw: do you have a simple SLA template?
[07:47] Alex Chen: yes we'll attach a draft SLA covering availability, SLOs for model-serving latency targets, and incident response.
[07:53] Maya Lopez: any red flags on network egress or regional availability? Meridian uses eu-west for data residency, we can run pilot there.
[07:59] Tom Wallace: yes, eu-west is critical. we need to ensure region-level capacity and failover.
[08:05] Jordan Patel: noted. we'll validate regional capacity and include a failover plan (fallback to another EU region).
[08:12] Dana Ruiz: great. for the benchmarking harness, do you capture tokenization variance? our tokenizer sometimes splits emojis and special chars weirdly which affects token counts.
[08:22] Maya Lopez: we ingest your tokenizer or use our tokenizer spec that matches model family. we'll run a tokenization pass on sample payloads to get accurate token histograms.
[08:30] Priya Kaur: any guidance on how to simulate client behavior for chat vs batch?
[08:34] Jordan Patel: chat: simulate fan-out with many short requests, include think-time per user; batch: steady(rate) large inputs with long outputs. we'll provide a runner config.
[08:43] Alex Chen: last thing - can you confirm cost objective again? 0.70 per 1k tokens is the threshold?
[08:49] Dana Ruiz: yes, averaged across workload. if pilot shows 0.85, procurement will push back.
[08:55] Jordan Patel: understood. we'll include cost sensitivity analysis.
[09:00] Alex Chen: wrap up - action items and timeline are in the next steps. any final clarifications?
[09:05] Tom Wallace: none from me, we'll start pulling logs.
[09:07] Dana Ruiz: thanks all, looking forward.

[62:00] End of call
